ambiguities.text: The specification uses 'fake_block_number' without explicitly defining the complete difficulty calculation formula that uses this value
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the fake_block_number is used in the standard Ethereum difficulty adjustment algorithm (EIP-2) where it affects the exponential difficulty increase component. This needs cross-reference with the base difficulty specification.

ambiguities.text: The term 'approximately 7.5 months' delay is mentioned without precise block time assumptions
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the calculation is based on ~13.3 second average block time. The exact delay depends on actual network conditions.

implicit_assumptions.description: Network hashrate remains relatively stable so that the bomb delay timing estimates hold
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If hashrate drops significantly, the difficulty bomb effects could manifest earlier than expected, causing longer block times before the next fork can address it

implicit_assumptions.description: All clients will upgrade before the fork block number is reached
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Chain split between upgraded and non-upgraded clients due to different difficulty calculations

implicit_assumptions.description: The offset value (10,700,000) is correctly chosen to provide adequate delay for planned network upgrades
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Insufficient delay could require emergency hard fork; excessive delay removes upgrade pressure
